senses.gloss: (b. h.; cmp. כָּהָה)to be dull, blunt; (of a sword) to slide off a hard object.
units: <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 9:1:14">Y. Ber. IX, 13ᵃ</cite> <he>וקָהַת החרב מעל וכ׳</he> and the sword slid off Moses’ neck and broke; <cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 2">Deut. R. s. 2</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 167:3">Yalk. Ex. 167</cite> <he>וקהית</he> (corr. acc.).

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 78">Gen. R. s. 78</cite>; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 7:5">Cant. R. to VII, 5</cite> <he>וקָהוּ שיניו וכ׳</he> and the teeth of the wicked (Esau) became blunt and loose.
Num. R. s. 3 (ref. to Koh. X, 10) אם ראית שקהו השמים וכ׳, v. preced.—Trnsf. to be difficult, unsolvable.

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:7">Cant. R. to III, 7</cite> <he>שהיו כולן שונין … הלכה קוֹהָא להם</he> they all sharpened the discussion like a sword, so that, when a case came before them, the decision might not be too difficult for them.
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 4:4:7">Ib. to IV, 4</cite> <he>שאין הלכה קוהא להם</he> never was there a subject too difficult for them to decide; a. e.

senses.gloss: to be wearied; to faint; esp. to have a morbid appetite (caused by the smell of a dish). Ib. to I, 12 the Lord sent them a sweet scent from Eden והיתה נפשם קוהא לאכול and they were dying to eat (of the Passover sacrifice), v. עָיֵף; a. e.
(with שן) to make blunt and loose; trnsf. to refute; to break the power of; to grieve. Mekh. Bo, s. 18 אף אתה הַקְהֵה את שיניו thou, too, make his teeth blunt (refute his arguments).
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 99:8">Gen. R. s. 99</cite> (play on <he>יקהת</he>, <cite ref="Genesis 49:10">Gen. XLIX, 10</cite>) <he>מי שמַקְהֶה שני וכ׳</he> he (the Messiah) that shall break the power of all nations; <cite ref="Genesis 49:10">ib.</cite> s. 98.

<cite ref="Sotah 49a">Sot. 49ᵃ</cite> [read:] <he>אומרים … למה הִקְהִיתָ וכ׳</he> (v. Rashi) they (the children of the wicked that died in their parents’ lifetime) argue before him, … if thou intendedst to punish them in the hereafter, why didst thou cause them grief while living? <cite ref="Sotah 49a">Ib.</cite> <he>שמחת … והקהית השיני</he> thou hast gladdened my heart (with the evidence of thy purity) and given me pain (by showing more affection for thy son than for myself).
<cite ref="Sanhedrin 109b:13">Snh. 109ᵇ</cite> (play on <he>בן קהת</he>, <cite ref="Numbers 16:1">Num. XVI, 1</cite>) <he>בן שה׳ וכ׳</he> a son that brought grief over his parents; a. e.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 10:10:1">Koh. R. to X, 10</cite> <he>אם נִקְהֵת אומה וכ׳</he> if the nation whose power was as hard as iron, has grown powerless.

senses.gloss: to be tough, difficult. Ib. אם נ׳ תלמודך וכ׳ if thy lesson is as tough to thee as iron (v. preced).

units: <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 186:1">Yalk. Ex. 186</cite> (ref. to <he>מתלקחת</he>, <cite ref="Exodus 9:24">Ex. IX, 24</cite>) <he>מִתְקָהָא לעשות שליחותה</he> (not <he>שליחותיה</he>) it (the fire) was dying to perform its mission; Pesik. Vayhi, p. 4ᵃ <he>מיתה מתקהא וכ׳</he> Ar. (ed. <he>מתקריא</he>, corr. acc.) dying, that is longing &c.; <cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 3:11:1">Cant. R. to III, 11</cite> <he>מיתה ומתקלהא בשביל לעשות רצון בוראם</he> (corr. acc., a. read <he>בוראה</he>); <cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 12">Num. R. s. 12</cite> (combining both versions) <he>מיתה ומתקהלא לעשות … בוראה</he> (corr. acc.).

senses.gloss: to become tough, hard, unyielding, grievous, irksome. Koh. R. l. c. אם נִתְקָהוּ שמים שעל וכ׳ if the heavens above you have become hard as iron &c., v. supra. Ib. אם נתק׳ הרב על התלמיד וכ׳ if the teacher has been unyielding to the pupil like iron (out of patience, and refusing to teach him) …, and the teacher shows not a friendly face (does not relent) &c. Ib. אם נתק׳ התלמיד על הרב וכ׳ if the pupil has been annoying to his teacher (through his obtuseness or wearisome questions) …, and the teacher refuses to explain &c.
